clue.text: Capital walk can end up miles from Cambridge

indicators.note: taking something from a word leaves the rest of it behind, so a letter is subtracted here
the remaining letters can end up in a different order, so they are to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A stroll in London that wanders off and ends up a long way from Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of CAMBRIDGE to leave CABRIDGE, then rearrange it. Birdcage Walk is a street in London beside St James's Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is a named street in the British capital, close to Buckingham Palace, so the first word fills the blank.

clue.text: Break into the Iberian nosh-up

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the letters climb from bottom to top, reading backwards

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
nosh and grub are both slang for food

explanation.surface: Gatecrashing a Spanish feast.
explanation.walkthrough: Nosh-up is British slang for a big meal; split it and up becomes the instruction to turn the pieces over.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgle is to break into a building to steal, so the phrasal verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sturdy or else broken

indicators.note: else means otherwise, so the short word is to be put another way

blocks.note: taken as written
bust is informal for broken

explanation.surface: Something is either sturdy or it is broken: no middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and hardy, able to withstand knocks, so it is a direct synonym of sturdy.

clue.text: Animal doctor dissecting 20 in Canterbury, say

indicators.note: dissecting means cutting into, so one piece cuts into the middle of another

blocks.note: a cat is an animal
20 is REMEDY; to remedy is to heal
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A vet operating on a cure in Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal doctor looks like one phrase meaning vet, but it splits in two. Canterbury is a city in Kent, famous for its great church.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury has a famous cathedral, and 'say' marks the city as an example of where one is found.

clue.text: Replaced lagging round that which shocks

indicators.note: replaced means put back differently, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber renews the insulation around an electric cable that gives shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagging is British for insulation wrapped round pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Guignol was a Paris theatre of gory horror, so the term means sensational drama designed to horrify audiences.

clue.text: Where to see supporters scoffing at back?

definitions.text: Where to see supporters scoffing at back?

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so one word swallows the other
going back means the whole combination is read from right to left

blocks.note: aids are things that support or help
taken as written

explanation.surface: Where would you find fans tucking into food in the back rows?
explanation.walkthrough: Supporters does double duty: it is the wordplay's helpers and, read with the whole clue, the fans whom sports grounds hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports grounds are the places where crowds of fans gather to watch and cheer their teams.

clue.text: Furthermore, lacks great enthusiasm for measure

indicators.note: a word that lacks something is missing letters, so these are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
a furore is an outburst of enthusiasm or excitement

explanation.surface: Moreover, someone is short of passion for a plan of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FURORE are spread through the first word: FUR at the front and ORE at the end; remove both.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat used in billing gas, so it is a measure of quantity.

clue.text: Moor's enemy breaks up ground that's sloping

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is read from bottom to top
something that breaks another goes into it, splitting it open

blocks.note: land is ground
Iago is Othello's enemy in Shakespeare; Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An enemy of the Moors digging up ground on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Moor suggests heathland, but it is Othello, the Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line runs at a slant between corners, so it is sloping rather than level or upright.

clue.text: High position is titled - au contraire

indicators.note: contraire, French for contrary, means going the opposite way, so the order is overturned

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being an aristocrat gives you a lofty social position; or, on the contrary, perhaps it doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase au contraire splits: its first word is letters, its second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Altitude is height above sea level, so a high position in the air is a great elevation.

clue.text: Checking concrete case for cask

indicators.note: a case surrounds what it holds, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: concrete in the sense of actual or tangible
a butt is a large barrel

explanation.surface: A builder inspects the concrete casing poured around a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal checks or counters an argument, so checking, as a noun of opposition, means a refutation.

clue.text: Go for record-breaking run

indicators.note: something breaking into another sits inside it, splitting it apart

blocks.note: to dart is to run quickly
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An athlete sets off on an attempt at a record-breaking run.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or set off, a straightforward synonym for the verb go.

clue.text: English port with nothing doing for renal expert

indicators.note: doing means working on, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A coastal town in England where a kidney specialist has nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, and a nephrologist is the medical specialist who treats them.

clue.text: Long Island's yarn

blocks.note: L is an abbreviation for long
an isle is an island

explanation.surface: A tale told about Long Island in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Long Island looks like a single place name, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread, so it is a kind of yarn used for stockings.

clue.text: Perfect mate on board?

blocks.note: surface reading: an ideal partner, the one you would choose above all others
setter's reading: the question mark hints at a vessel, as if the ideal partner were a ship

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into a fantasy and a vessel, so the ideal partner becomes a craft you might sail aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is informal for a very attractive person, the perfect romantic partner someone longs for.

clue.text: 18 where men can become kings

blocks.note: surface reading: a battlefield where soldiers may win a crown
setter's reading: in draughts, the pieces are called men and are crowned kings on reaching the far side

explanation.surface: A war in which ordinary soldiers might rise to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BATTLEGROUND. Draughts is the British name for checkers, where a piece reaching the far row becomes a king.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkered playing surface for draughts is where the game's contest takes place, and promoted pieces are crowned there.

clue.text: What's got on when trying to get on

definitions.text: What's got on when trying to get on

blocks.note: surface reading: something boarded, like a bus or train
setter's reading: getting ahead by joining a popular trend, climbing aboard a vehicle in the idiom

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is jumping on the bandwagon: joining a popular cause to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: People climb onto a fashionable movement to succeed, the vehicle of the idiom for following a trend.

clue.text: Purloin anything but concrete

blocks.note: first meaning: to steal or remove, a formal verb
second meaning: theoretical, existing only as an idea

explanation.walkthrough: Purloin looks like the odd one out, but the verb sense means to take away or steal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to remove or steal; as an adjective it means conceptual rather than tangible.

clue.text: Hold up particle used in stud

blocks.note: to stall is to delay, to hold up
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of something jams up a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud looks like a fastening or earring, but it is a breeding establishment for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm keeps uncastrated male horses for breeding, so the stud is where such a horse is put to use.

clue.text: Be in the first parts of contest - that's where it's at

blocks.clueFragment: Be in the first parts of
blocks.note: surface reading: take part in the opening stages of a competition
setter's reading: the place where a fight happens is its site

explanation.surface: Advice to get involved early in a competition because that is where the action is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as a fight plus the spot on which it stands: a contest and where it is at.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleground is the site where a fight or struggle is waged, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Quiet girl lifted film

indicators.note: in a down light, lifted means raised from bottom to top, so read backwards

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical instruction for quiet
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy young woman is caught taking a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Film suggests cinema, but here it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface layer formed by age, like the green coat on bronze, so a film.

clue.text: Fix molten lead in piping

indicators.note: the lead of a word is what goes at the front, so its first letter is taken
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: piping as in high-pitched and thin, like a reed instrument
first letter

explanation.surface: A plumber repairs melted lead inside a set of pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: Molten lead reads like plumbing metal, but lead here picks out a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy something is to set it right or repair it, so the verb is a synonym of fix.

clue.text: Stroke to the pole that long shots require

indicators.note: a stroke is a sweeping movement, and stroking these words moves their letters around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower or swimmer pushing on towards the North Pole in a feat of endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Long shots looks like gambling or distance, but here it means photographs taken from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens magnifies distant subjects, so photographers need one for pictures taken from far off.

clue.text: Smoother sound is clear

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so we want a word spoken the same

blocks.note: a plane is a carpenter's tool that smooths wood

explanation.surface: A smoother sound comes through more clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoother looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: a tool that smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means obvious or easy to understand, as in plain to see, so it is a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Bob's partner is bore about drug

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Bob's girlfriend is a tedious person who is always on about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name, but it is the boxing move, as in bob and weave.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a fighter will bob and weave, so the evasive sideways movement is the natural companion of bobbing.

clue.text: Beast with bony plate to rear

indicators.note: sending something to the rear turns it back to front, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer, as of bone

explanation.surface: A creature with a protective armoured plate on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, especially a four-legged one, so the general term for a living creature fits.

clue.text: Call team for good spot at 18

blocks.note: to ring is to telephone, or call
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Phoning the squad to tell them about a good position on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BATTLEGROUND; a boxing match is a fight, and the ringside seats are the best places to watch it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are right beside the boxing ring, the prime viewing position for a fight.

clue.text: One in covering letter has one

indicators.note: one item placed inside another sits within it

blocks.note: a tent is a canvas covering
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An enclosure in a covering letter is mentioned as one item.
explanation.walkthrough: Covering letter suggests a note sent with a CV, but here the letter is someone who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who lets a property is a letter, and the person renting from them is their occupant.

clue.text: Good girl with a line that's mine

blocks.note: ST, saint, a good person
a girl's name
the a taken as written
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A man boasts that a well-behaved girl with a chat-up line is his.
explanation.walkthrough: Mine looks like a possessive, but it is the noun. A stannary was a tin-mining district in Cornwall and Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannary means a tin mine or tin-mining region, from Latin stannum for tin, so it is a specific mine.
